notes: Source is the SAME patent as p300.json/p400.json: US 6,115,188 ("Optical system and optical apparatus having the same", Canon Kabushiki Kaisha; priority 10/16/1997, filed 10/14/1998, published 9/5/2000). Numerical Example 10 (f=490.93, Fno=4.1, 2w=5.0deg) is used here for the 500 mm slot.

Same 'D(last)=0.000 is a table-terminator, not the real Bf' finding as p300.json/p400.json. The terminal surface's t is DERIVED from our own paraxial trace, not patent-stated; stated.bf is intentionally omitted.
Aperture stop printed explicitly as 'R14 = Stop', transcribed at surface index 13 (0-based) as a flat, zero-power reference surface, same as the other two lenses in this family.

Rear-group cementing differs again from both other examples: R23/R24 (index 22-23, L3d) are NOT cemented here (genuine air gap D24=5.00), unlike Example 1's equivalent doublet. Transcribed exactly as printed; each example in this patent varies its own internal grouping, which is expected (they are independently optimized designs sharing an architecture, not scaled copies of each other).

This example has only ONE flat air-gap surface before the filter (index 25, r=null, t=30.00) rather than the extra labeled 'fixed stop HP' surface seen in Example 7 (p400.json) -- transcribed exactly as printed, no forced consistency across examples.

Focus: same shared-patent inner-focus description (L2 moves for focusing). This numerical example likewise gives only the infinity-focus D values; no close-focus variable gap is printed, so no VariableGap entries are recorded.

Elements/groups counted directly from the cemented-interface pattern: front L1 = 5 singlets (5 groups, 5 elements); L2 = 1 cemented doublet (1 group, 2 elements, inner-focus group); rear L3 = 2 doublets (L3a, L3b) + 3 singlets (L3c, L3d, L3e) = 5 groups, 7 elements; plus the filter block (1 group, 1 element). Total: elements = 5+2+7+1 = 15; groups = 5+1+5+1 = 12.

No effective/clear diameters are printed anywhere in this patent, so every sd is sdSource='estimated-from-marginal-ray' via .local/lens-tele/paraxial.py (same method as p300.json/p400.json: entrance-beam semi-diameter at surface 1 = EFL/(2*Fno), traced forward, plus the paraxial chief ray at the patent's own printed half field 2w=5.0deg/2=2.5deg). Placeholder sd=1 values below were overwritten by running that script -- see research/lenses-tele.md for the printed self-check numbers.

representativeOf intentionally left unset: no public source ties US 6,115,188 to a specific commercial product, despite the strong circumstantial match to Canon's original EF 500mm f/4L IS USM (July 1999) in focal length, Fno class and filing-to-release timing.
Lead 9/28/2026: elements/groups (14/11, was 15/12) count lens elements only; the drop-in filter plate is marked plate: "drop-in-filter" and is not an element or a group.
